idea-plugin.name: Seshlog - Coding Agent Session Manager
idea-plugin.description:
List, search and resume your local Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Pi sessions from a tool window, titled the way the agent titles them, with one click to reopen any of them in a terminal tab.

  • Sessions grouped by project with title, branch, last activity and a live indicator
  • Follow Claude Code and Codex sessions across recorded worktree changes, with checkout paths, observed Git branches and detached-HEAD labels
  • Open a session's verified worktree in a new IntelliJ window or focus it if already open, keeping the original window and terminal available. Opening is disabled for missing or uncertain checkouts and for new projects inside protected agent data directories.
  • Open Worktree and Fork Session starts an independent conversation fork in the worktree window's terminal, keeping the original session running.
  • Compact per-project Agents menu: show any combination of available agents, with your last selection restored when the project opens
  • Search titles, working directories and conversations by relevance, with quoted phrases for exact matches
  • Choose which messages and tool activity can match, with conversation-only search by default and clear labels showing where each result matched
  • Reuse the local search index across restarts, with controls to rebuild, clear, export and import it
  • Preview recent messages or inspect the full loaded conversation for a search result, with highlighted matches and keyboard navigation
  • Resume or fork a session into a new terminal tab; focus the tab if it is already running
  • Copy the latest assistant reply from Claude Code, Codex, opencode or Pi, preserving Markdown and code blocks without selecting terminal output
  • Copy the latest identifiable plan from Claude Code or Codex for review elsewhere
  • Use both copy actions from a known session's terminal, the session list or the conversation viewer; assign your own shortcuts in Settings → Keymap
  • Restore the sessions that were running when the IDE was closed
  • Activity badges and waiting notifications show when an agent needs input
  • Unread reply markers and next-attention navigation help you follow concurrent sessions
  • Pin, locally rename or hide sessions without modifying agent data
  • Filter by date, agent and sibling worktrees
Entirely local: Seshlog reads the agent's transcripts read-only, never writes to them, and makes no network requests — no telemetry, no analytics, nothing leaves your machine. The saved search index contains sensitive lexical terms and positions, without raw conversation copies or query history. Export and import are explicit; indexes are never uploaded automatically.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.8.1
  • Choose Your messages, Assistant replies and Tool activity from Search in. Conversation is the default, with tools excluded; session titles and working directories always remain searchable. Remember the choice across project windows and IDE restarts.
  • Show whether each result matched a title, project path, user message, assistant reply, tool call or tool result. Open the supporting passage and keep search highlights and next/previous navigation within the selected sources, while leaving the full conversation available.
  • Fix technical and quoted matches being overlooked when a partial title or path match ranks higher, and start preview next/previous navigation from the passage that was opened.
  • Reduce repeated text processing when checking matches, making ordinary searches and repeated tool output faster.
  • Upgrading from 0.8.0 requires a one-time local search-index rebuild to enable source classification. Keep the previous saved index until you choose Rebuild in Search settings, and use temporary filtered search in the meantime.
0.8.0
  • Rank search results by relevance across session titles, local title overrides, working directories and conversation passages. Ordinary query terms can match independently; quoted phrases require exact text.
  • Keep a local search index across IDE restarts and update changed sessions incrementally. Search runs entirely on your machine without a model or network connection.
  • Open search results at the supporting conversation passage, expand matching tool entries, and reject stale passage locations when the source changes. Show partial search coverage even when there are no matches.
  • Manage the search index under Settings → Tools → Seshlog → Search: refresh, retry, rebuild, clear, export or import it. Saved indexes contain sensitive lexical terms and positions, without raw conversation copies or query history.
  • Fix importing valid search indexes with many dense passages, preserving existing local entries.
0.7.1
  • Add Open Worktree and Fork Session: open or focus the session's worktree window and start a separate conversation fork in a new terminal there. Preserve the recorded subdirectory and leave the original session running.
  • Recheck the checkout and session location before launching the fork. Cancelled opens, closed windows and missing or changed directories do not start a session in the wrong place.
0.6.10
  • Show Claude Code and Codex session worktrees with checkout details, the observed Git branch or detached HEAD, and the full recorded path in tooltips.
  • Follow recorded working-directory changes as sessions move between checkouts. Project filtering and the Sibling worktrees option use the updated location in both browsing and search.
  • Open a session's verified worktree in a new IntelliJ window, or focus the window already using it. The original project window and its agent terminals stay open.
  • Keep missing or uncertain worktrees visible while disabling opening. New project opening inside protected agent data directories remains disabled; an already-open project there can still be focused.
0.6.9
  • Track Codex terminals again from codex-cli 0.158, which runs sessions through a shared background server rather than the terminal's own process. Seshlog matches each Codex terminal to the session that server has open for the same directory, so new Codex sessions attach to their tab, relaunching Codex in a tab attaches it again, and copying a reply or plan works in tabs started with a plain codex command.
  • Attach only when that match is unambiguous across every Codex terminal on the machine, including those outside the IDE. Several Codex tabs in one directory are told apart by when each started its session, so they no longer all stay unattached; two started within seconds of each other still do rather than risk copying from the wrong one. A resumed Codex tab follows a new session started inside Codex once Codex has closed the previous one.
  • Own a forked session's tab from the moment it opens, as for a new session, so it attaches to the fork, offers Fork and Copy, and is restored after a restart.
  • Resume a session in the tab its agent last exited in, even after the session was renamed, and bring a reused tab to the front instead of opening another.
  • Recognise Codex terminal transcripts written by the new server, including sessions run with --no-daemon.
